rejected.section: Getting sync right (why this won't repeat the Firebase problem)
rejected.fact: Ticks set a value; they don't flip it. The tick action is `setChecked(itemId, checked: boolean)`, not "toggle". If you both tap the same item, the result is still correct and stable. Instant feedback: every tick, add and reorder shows on screen immediately and then syncs. Server-side list building: combining the week's recipes into a shopping list happens in one transactional step on the server. Rebuilding the list keeps ticked items, manual items and edits, and only adds, removes or adjusts the items that came from recipes. Connection indicator: a small dot shows "Live / Reconnecting / Offline – changes will sync". Changes made while offline are held and sent when you reconnect. In the store: the shopping screen keeps the phone awake, ticked items drop to the bottom of their aisle, and each tick shows who made it ("✓ by Rory").

The `invites` document has fields: `householdId`, `code`, and `expiresAt`. The `recipes` document has fields: `householdId`, `title`, `description`, `servings`, `prepMin`, `cookMin`, `tags[]`, `cuisine`, `source` (with kind: generated|url|instagram|photo|manual, url?), `glutenFree`, `glutenNotes?`, `ingredients[]` (with id, qty, unit, name, canonical, aisle, note?, optional?, glutenRisk, gfSwap?), `steps[]` (with id, text, timers[] {label, seconds}, ingredientIds[]), and `nutritionPerServing` (with kcal, protein, carbs, fat, fibre).

The `ratings` document has fields: `recipeId`, `userId`, `stars` (1–5), `wouldCookAgain`, `comment?`, and `cookedAt`. The `tasteProfile` document has fields: `likes[]` and `dislikes[]` (ingredients or cuisines), `spiceLevel`, `notes`, and `summary`. The `summary` is rewritten by Claude from ratings, comments and dislikes every few ratings and is included in every generation prompt. The `pantry` document has fields: `householdId`, `name`, `canonical`, `qty?`, `unit?`, `useSoon` (boolean), and `addedAt). Ticking a shopping item can move it into the pantry (optional). "Mark recipe cooked" offers to remove the pantry items it used up.

result.summary: The GRKN is an application designed to help partners decide what to cook each week and find new, nutritious recipes. It manages household details, meal planning, and shopping list creation through a connected backend.

key_points.section: Plan: The GRKN – shared meal-planning app for two

key_points.fact: The app addresses the problem of partners deciding what to cook each week.
Every query updates live on both phones with Convex.

key_points.section: Getting sync right (why this won't repeat the Firebase problem)
key_points.fact: Each shopping item is its own document.

key_points.section: Claude integration (`convex/ai.ts`, a Node server function)
key_points.fact: The Claude integration uses the `@anthropic-ai/sdk` with structured output for valid, typed recipes.
The scale factor is planned servings divided by recipe servings to combine ingredients by `canonical`.
The fourth step is to build the week calendar, which includes breakfast (optional, repeatable), lunch and dinner, plus the 'Build shopping list' feature which combines and tests the list.

key_points.section: Keeping the build efficient (Claude Code token use)
key_points.fact: The build process should use official generators like `create-next-app`, `npx convex dev`, `shadcn add`, and `@convex-dev/auth` init instead of writing boilerplate by hand.
A fixed set of 10 prompts and imports must return correct glutenRisk flags for gluten checks.
